summary:
Terra Detective is an interactive web application that helps people explore how Earth is changing using NASA data from 2000 to 2025. Users select a location on a globe to investigate temperature, rainfall, and soil moisture trends through accessible maps and simple explanations.

To address the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, we combine NASA’s MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, and GLDAS datasets with statistical analysis that accounts for seasonal patterns and autocorrelation. Two statistical tests assess whether the evidence supports a trend. Results include comparisons between earlier and recent years, a five-step explanation of the analysis, and a coin-flip analogy that makes statistical uncertainty easier to understand.

Our prototype makes complex Earth science accessible to students, farmers, and families without requiring technical expertise or specialized equipment. By clearly showing both detected trends and inconclusive results, Terra Detective supports climate education and informed conversations about water, agriculture, and adaptation.
details:
Terra Detective is an interactive web application that turns NASA Earth science data into understandable evidence about environmental change. It helps users investigate three questions: What has changed in a location? By how much? And how strong is the evidence?

HOW IT WORKS

Users explore a globe and select a location to examine temperature, rainfall, or soil moisture. The application displays trends on a shared 2° grid covering 16,200 cells worldwide, using records within the 2000–2025 period. A result card compares averages for 2000–2009 and 2016–2025 and explains the observed change in everyday language.

The analysis removes the seasonal cycle and fits a linear trend with a 95% confidence interval. It adjusts the regression-based significance test for autocorrelation and also applies a seasonal Mann–Kendall test, with Sen’s slope providing a robust estimate of change. A trend is classified as statistically significant when both tests meet the selected significance threshold. When evidence is insufficient, the application clearly reports that no trend has been established.

A five-step explanation lets users follow the analysis from the original observations to the final result. A coin-flip analogy illustrates how unlikely a result would be under a no-trend assumption, making statistical significance more approachable without requiring users to interpret technical notation.

NASA DATA AND DEVELOPMENT TOOLS

The project uses MERRA-2 near-surface air temperature from NASA GMAO, GPM IMERG precipitation from NASA and JAXA, and GLDAS-2.1 Noah topsoil moisture. These products combine satellite observations, other measurements, and models in different ways.

A Python pipeline retrieves and processes monthly data using earthaccess, xarray, NumPy, and SciPy. NASA Earthdata services and OPeNDAP allow the pipeline to request the variables it needs. Processed results are exported as lightweight JSON files, while monthly time series are divided into geographic tiles so the browser loads only the relevant area.

The interface uses JavaScript, HTML, CSS, D3.js, TopoJSON, and canvas. Statistical calculations also run in the browser, with automated tests checking consistency between Python and JavaScript results. Development and delivery tools include Google Colab, pytest, Node.js tests, GitHub Actions, and GitHub Pages. Claude was used as an AI development assistant. Users need only a standard web browser on a phone or computer.

CREATIVITY AND BENEFITS

Our main creative contribution is connecting scientific analysis with a detective-style experience. Users can move from a global overview to a local result and then inspect the evidence behind it. Comparisons between earlier and recent years, plain-language explanations, and the coin-flip analogy make complex methods easier to explore.

Terra Detective is intended to help students learn about trends and uncertainty, support teachers with real NASA data, and help farmers and families understand regional environmental changes. It provides a starting point for informed discussions about agriculture, water use, and adaptation.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS AND LIMITATIONS

We prioritized accessibility, transparency, reproducibility, and small downloads. The interface communicates inconclusive findings as clearly as significant trends.

We also considered the limits of the evidence. A 2° cell represents a broad area and cannot describe individual farms. The available period may be too short to detect some changes, and trends do not establish their causes. Testing thousands of cells also requires additional controls before global significance totals can be treated as definitive.

Next steps include completing the AI Detective integration, adding MODIS vegetation greenness, expanding language support, improving data masks, and testing the interface with users who have no technical background.
